question: What is the median of the data set 34, 14, 6, 22, 27?

question: In a survey, 150 students were asked whether they play an instrument. Of the 80 ninth graders, 58 play an instrument; of the 70 tenth graders, 38 play an instrument. If one of the students who play an instrument is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student is a ninth grader?
explanation: Only the 96 students who play an instrument count (58 + 38). Of those, 58 are ninth graders, so the probability is 58/96 = 29/48.

question: A park counted 140 dogs. Of the 50 large dogs, 32 were on a leash; of the 90 small dogs, 44 were on a leash. If one of the dogs on a leash is chosen at random, what is the probability that the dog is a large dog?
explanation: Only the 76 dogs on a leash count (32 + 44). Of those, 32 are large dogs, so the probability is 32/76 = 8/19. 16/25 answers a different question: what fraction of the large dogs are among the dogs on a leash.

question: A cafe served 90 customers. Of the 50 customers who ordered coffee, 27 also bought a pastry; of the 40 who ordered tea, 16 also bought a pastry. If one of the customers who bought a pastry is chosen at random, what is the probability that the customer ordered coffee?
explanation: Only the 43 customers who bought a pastry count (27 + 16). Of those, 27 are coffee drinkers, so the probability is 27/43 = 27/43. 27/50 answers a different question: what fraction of the coffee drinkers are among the customers who bought a pastry.

question: A clinic tracked 110 patients. Of the 80 patients who got the new treatment, 8 improved; of the 30 who got the standard treatment, 25 improved. If one of the patients who improved is chosen at random, what is the probability that the patient got the new treatment?
explanation: Only the 33 patients who improved count (8 + 25). Of those, 8 are new-treatment patients, so the probability is 8/33 = 8/33.

question: A school polled 120 seniors. Of the 80 seniors who drive to school, 43 have a part-time job; of the 40 who take the bus, 27 have a part-time job. If one of the seniors with a part-time job is chosen at random, what is the probability that the senior drives to school?

question: An orchard picked 120 apples. Of the 50 red apples, 15 were bruised; of the 70 green apples, 53 were bruised. If one of the bruised apples is chosen at random, what is the probability that the apple is red?
explanation: Only the 68 bruised apples count (15 + 53). Of those, 15 are red apples, so the probability is 15/68 = 15/68. 3/10 answers a different question: what fraction of the red apples are among the bruised apples.

question: A random sample of 200 of the 8,000 students at a school found that 62 of them walk to school. Based on the sample, about how many students at the school walk to school?
explanation: In the sample, 62/200 of the students have the trait. Applying that to all 8,000: (62/200) × 8,000 = 2,480.

question: A random sample of 50 voters out of 1,250 registered voters in a town showed that 10 support a new library. About how many registered voters support it?

question: The equation x² + y² + 8x − 2y + 8 = 0 defines a circle in the xy-plane. What is the radius of the circle?
explanation: Complete the square: (x + 4)² + (y − 1)² = 16 + 1 − 8 = 9. The radius is √9 = 3.

question: In a right triangle, one acute angle measures 38°, and sin(38°) ≈ 0.62. What is the approximate value of cos(52°)?
